districtFact: South-Western City Schools serves an unusually varied 119-square-mile section of Central Ohio: all of Grove City, parts of Columbus, and portions of Franklin, Jackson, Pleasant, and Prairie townships. One district calendar therefore coordinates urban, suburban, and rural school communities.
profileDisclaimer: Enrollment is approximate and comes from the district's current public profile. Individual schools and programs may publish building events, bell schedules, orientations, and emergency changes that are not part of the district calendar PDF.

about.title: K–3 Starts by Last-Name Group
about.content: Grades 4–12 begin together, but kindergarten through grade 3 students enter in three surname groups: A–G, H–O, then P–Z. This is a real attendance distinction, not an optional orientation, so younger families should use the matching date instead of the headline district start alone.

about.title: Six Calamity Dates Are Contingencies
about.content: Each reviewed PDF reserves six dates after the planned last student day. They are not automatic class days. SWCS may activate them only if lost instructional time requires a calendar extension, so they remain visible as conditional planning dates and are excluded from the default calendar import.

about.title: Election Day Has Two Different Labels
about.content: The November Election Day closure is printed as a regular no-school date. The May primary date is explicitly tentative and subject to the Board of Elections calendar. Families should confirm the May date before making a nonrefundable plan.

about.title: Grade Bands Shape the District
about.content: SWCS organizes its core schools as K–4 elementary, grades 5–6 intermediate, grades 7–8 middle, and grades 9–12 high school. The district also operates a career-technical academy for grades 11–12 and a special-needs preschool, so program-level dates can matter beyond the main attendance calendar.

about.title: The District Crosses City and Township Lines
about.content: The attendance area includes Grove City and parts of Columbus as well as Franklin, Jackson, Pleasant, and Prairie townships. The PDF is therefore the common planning layer across communities that may otherwise use different municipal services and local event schedules.

about.title: Language Access Extends Beyond Spanish
about.content: The district snapshot reports 81 languages spoken by students and identifies Spanish, Somali, Arabic, Ukrainian, and Hakha Chin among its most common home languages. SWCS currently links Spanish graphic calendars for the two future years reviewed here; families needing another language should use district interpretation resources.

calendarNotes: The SWCS district calendar is the baseline for districtwide student attendance. Grades 4–12 share the first day, while K–3 students begin according to the first letter of the student's last name. A professional day means no school for students even when staff report. November Election Day is a confirmed closure, while the May primary date is tentative and can move with the Board of Elections schedule. The four printed nine-week dates mark the beginning of grading periods rather than days off. Calamity Day Contingency Dates are reserved extensions after the scheduled last day and should not be treated as confirmed attendance. Spanish graphic calendars are official language resources, but building events, transportation notices, athletics, graduation ceremony times, and emergency revisions still require a school or district check.

planningTips.title: Planning with the South-Western City Schools Calendar
content: For a K–3 student, match the first letter of the student's last name to the A–G, H–O, or P–Z opening date; grades 4–12 use the first district date.
Keep the six post-year calamity dates as a travel buffer, but do not put them in a shared calendar as confirmed school days unless SWCS activates them.
Treat the November Election Day as a scheduled closure and the May primary date as tentative until the district confirms the county election schedule.
Use the nine-week dates for grade-report planning, not childcare planning; they are instructional days unless another calendar label closes school.
Open the Spanish graphic calendar from the same official calendar center when that is the more useful family resource.
Check the individual school for orientation, conferences, performances, athletics, testing, and graduation ceremony times.
An ICS download is a one-time copy. Recheck the official calendar page after weather closures or a revised election date.

districtFaqs.q: Is South-Western City School District the same as Westland High School?
districtFaqs.a: No. Westland is one SWCS high school. This page uses the district website and districtwide calendar rather than the Westland school subsite.

districtFaqs.q: Do all SWCS students start on the same day?
districtFaqs.a: No. Grades 4–12 start together. K–3 students use three consecutive surname-group dates: A–G, H–O, and P–Z.

districtFaqs.q: Are the SWCS calamity contingency dates confirmed school days?
districtFaqs.a: No. They are reserved dates after the planned last day and become attendance days only if the district activates them to recover lost time.

districtFaqs.q: Is the May SWCS Election Day closure final?
districtFaqs.a: Not necessarily. The PDF calls it tentative and says it is subject to the Board of Elections primary date. Confirm it before arranging travel or childcare.

districtFaqs.q: Does SWCS publish a Spanish school calendar?
districtFaqs.a: Yes. SWCS publishes Spanish graphic calendars. Use the Downloads section on the selected school-year page for that year's official version.

districtFaqs.q: Are nine-week grading-period dates days off?
districtFaqs.a: No. They mark the beginning of each grading period and do not close school unless a separate no-school label appears.

districtFaqs.q: Do career academy and preschool families need another calendar?
districtFaqs.a: Use the district calendar for districtwide dates, but check the program or school calendar for orientations, bell schedules, conferences, and other program-specific events.
